decision: Reject equal-distance heap-root shortcut: no meaningful observed end-to-end improvement. Production source restored; retain expanded tie/budget properties.

profile.scope: 20-second sampling of earlier 162x150 carrier diagnostic; not a whole-run profile
profile.interpretation: Nearest-position frontier is the dominant sampled CPU consumer. Increased legalizer event counts alone do not locate the CPU bottleneck.

experiment: FrontierHeap::replace_top directly replaces the root when successor distance and row index equal the old root; only one live node per row exists. Every visited node and quantization call remains accounted for.
workload: Carrier 162x150 diagnostic, granular-minor+vertical+estimator-first, interior order 0, failed-first, owned quality/cohesion, group faces usb_jtag/power/power_som/power_mon, bottom power_mon/bringup_modules/bringup_en_modules, 1024 joint states, 8 poses, 4096 frontier, 3 continuations, victim shapes and board_aux=owned-face-a1.000000. Same options as reviewed-policy-sampled run.
tests: Expanded exhaustive frontier properties from 48 to 80 width/height/anchor cases, including symmetric ties; every positive frontier budget below exhaustive grid size checks exact node consumption and accepted-prefix preservation. Child-halo and instrumented numerical precision suites passed with experiment; rerun on restored production recorded separately.
restored_production_tests: Both suites PASS, 6.61 seconds total; native/build/heap-tie-restored-tests.log. Production generator and profiler rebuilt with shortcut removed.
limitations: Single screening pair; baseline briefly overlapped compilation/testing. No statistically supported speedup, smaller accepted board, full qualification, or Python comparison is claimed. Sample is partial and contains inlined work. Next optimization should address frontier traversal volume/data structure cost rather than assume event counts directly represent CPU cost.
